Day 64 of 100 · Docker

Docker Container Lifecycle

#100DaysOfCloudAndSecurityDockerPublished artifact recovered

A container combines an image with runtime configuration, a primary process and a writable layer whose lifecycle differs from both the image and durable storage.

Architecture / mental model

image → create/start container → PID 1 runs → process exits → container stopped → start again OR remove writable layer

How it works

A container remains running while its primary process remains alive. When that process exits, the container moves to an exited state even though the image still exists.

`docker stop` requests graceful termination, normally beginning with SIGTERM before a later forced signal if the process does not exit. `docker kill` sends a forceful signal by default and bypasses graceful application shutdown.

Stopping is not removing. Starting the same stopped container preserves its writable layer; removing the container discards that writable layer while leaving the underlying image unchanged.

Hands-on reference

docker run -d --name core-shield-web nginx:alpine
docker logs core-shield-web
docker exec -it core-shield-web sh
docker stop core-shield-web
docker start core-shield-web
docker rm core-shield-web
docker run --rm busybox:stable echo 'temporary task'

Verification

Create a disposable file in a container writable layer, stop/start the same container and confirm it remains. Then remove/recreate the container from the same image and confirm that writable-layer state is gone.

Field note / gotcha

Shell-form ENTRYPOINT or CMD can place the application behind `/bin/sh`, which may not forward termination signals correctly. PID 1 and signal handling matter for clean shutdown.

Security considerations

Do not store secrets or durable application state in the writable layer. Scope `docker exec` access because entering a running container is operationally powerful.

What I learned

Image, container and volume have different lifecycles. Reliability starts when you stop treating them as one thing.
